title: OpenIE Stack Desk: Shannon, von Neumann, and Hurwicz on One Substrate
subtitle: Elena, Liam, and Arthur show how information theory, game theory, and mechanism design lock together when computation pays joules
summary: At the OpenIE Stack Desk (stack.openie.dev), Elena, Liam, and Arthur connect Shannon-Landauer bit thermodynamics, von Neumann-Nash strategic interaction, and Hurwicz-Maskin-Myerson incentive-compatible commit gates (11,428 pJ on KV260) across nine Periodic Stacks, handoff verification, and Jevons task satiation.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to the OpenIE Stack Desk on OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Elena, joined by Liam and senior fellow Arthur — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced with ElevenLabs studio neural speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we open stack.openie.dev: Shannon, von Neumann, and Hurwicz on one substrate.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Arthur, in universities, physicists study Shannon and Landauer while economists study von Neumann and Hurwicz across campus! Give us an everyday picture of why they're actually three altitudes of the same machine.

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Picture a busy city suspension bridge, Liam! Down in the steel cables, engineers calculate load limits and dissipation — that is Claude Shannon and Rolf Landauer, counting bits and the two point eight seven one times ten to the minus twenty-one joule floor paid whenever a bit is irreversibly erased at room temperature.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now move up onto the roadway deck, where thousands of rush-hour drivers are choosing lanes!

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: On the deck, goal-holding agents react strategically to each other — that is John von Neumann and John Nash's game theory. And at the entrance plaza sits the tollbooth and axle scale: Leonid Hurwicz, Eric Maskin, and Roger Myerson's mechanism design, shaping the admission rules so honesty and safety beat bluffing!

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Wait — that tollbooth explains why unverified chat models hallucinate! If guessing confidently pays the same reward as verifying a patch, bluffing wins!

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Precisely! Metered Commit Gates place a physical Hurwicz mechanism right before state mutation: nothing irreversible commits until a deterministic check passes. On a Xilinx Kria KV260 module metered via an inline INA260 shunt, one gate cycle costs just eleven thousand four hundred twenty-eight picojoules of board-metered energy!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: How does stack.openie.dev map every computing workload across those three altitudes?

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Every computational act sums primitive counts times hardware joule weights across nine Periodic Stacks, partitioned into three zones: Zone One for deterministic lookup and checking, Zone Two for bounded search and routing, and Zone Three for open-world frontier synthesis.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Prove to a skeptic why we need all three zones instead of running pure Zone One lookup or pure Zone Three neural!

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Deterministic Null tested both across four thousand thirty held-out instances! On bounded formal Track-A classes, single-turn neural models failed to beat Zone One integer lookup on nine of ten cells. On open public benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified where lookup hits zero, Zone Three added up to ninety-five percentage points — and crystallizing verified outputs back into Zone One cut repeat energy spend three point five nine times!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now connect that to The Three-Body Problem in Computing — why do catastrophic failures cluster at multi-party handoffs?

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Because specifiers, builders, and users rely on unwritten assumptions — like Mars Climate Orbiter's unit mismatch or Ariane 5's float overflow! Checking static Forms and manifests caught ninety-eight point four six percent of one hundred thirty injected handoff faults versus near-zero for syntax parsing.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: And economically, you refuse to blend survey guesses into audited losses, while warning that cheaper tasks still trigger Jevons rebound!

turns.speaker: Arthur
turns.role: Senior Cryptography & Foundations Fellow · North American Senior
turns.text: Exactly. Each bounded job hits task satiation the moment its verifier passes, yet cheaper completions unlock new jobs economy-wide. Token prices fall, while physics guarantees electricity is never free.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Shannon sets the bit floor, von Neumann maps the players, and Hurwicz gates the commit. Explore stack.openie.dev, and join Mei, Nia, and Tariq next at the OpenIE Compute Desk!
